I think Young Legacy would not have a different enough deck from Finest Legacy to warrant being a full-blown hero. But absolutely there’s going to be a variant somewhere…!

This discussion got me thinking about how the expansions are getting thematically adjusted/expanded for Definitive Edition. For example, before the campaign I had been thinking of DE Disparation as the equivalent of EE Shattered Timelines, with a theme of time travel and alternate realities. But as the campaign progressed it became very clear that the theme isn’t “alternate realities” so much as it is “other realms” more broadly, which is how you get stuff like the Ennead or Aeternus in there. Perhaps instead of thinking about the subject matter genre of the remaining content (cosmic vs. magical and whatnot), it makes a lot of sense to think about broader thematic groupings. Something like “villains ascendant” might easily fit things like not only the Vengeful Five, but the Bloodsworn Collosseum or even Chokepoint or Wager Master.

I think a big question is what they’re going to do with the EE Villains of the Multiverse content. The team villain mode always felt pretty rough and weird to me. My hope might be to have several of them upgraded to full villain decks. And it doesn’t escape my notice that La Capitan’s deck has some of her previous Villains incarnation merged in…so maybe she or Plague Rat wouldn’t have a Villains-style version at all? There are also some new mechanics that they could take advantage of to give smaller/side villains like Greazer a place in a larger game, like as a side deck.

But if the DE equivalent of EE VotM isn’t the “team mode set” but is a more broad “villains” set, there are a number of other ways that set could take shape.

Perhaps the next one would be a “prelude” set forming the buildup to OblivAeon - containing things like Void Guard, the Celestial Tribunal, Deadline, and Progeny. “Cosmic Convergence,” perhaps?
